articles.title: Singapore’s foundations predate the LKY myth
articles.idea: Founder stories compress path dependence. The island’s free-port design, legal rails, and entrepôt role were already old when independence arrived in 1965.

articles.title: Forest City and Network School: capital meets host politics
articles.idea: Mega-projects fail politically when tenant cultures and host-state legitimacy diverge. Johor’s Forest City is a case of capital, immigration politics, and imported communities colliding.

articles.title: Network School as a Silicon Valley bubble in ASEAN
articles.idea: Importing SV norms into ASEAN sites can create value for mobile founders and friction for host politics. Talent density and enclave are two readings of the same room.

articles.title: Chinese diaspora parallel economies in host countries
articles.idea: Parallel commercial ecosystems can be resilience and political flashpoint at once. Formal national markets and ethnic network rails are not the same map.

articles.title: ASEAN is a portfolio of country tests, not one market
articles.idea: Regional rhetoric outruns operating reality. First-country choice is an experiment-design problem: buyer, trust bridge, compliance, payments, reusable model.

articles.title: US–China tech controls as market-entry parameters for SEA founders
articles.idea: Export controls and model-compute limits are not background noise. They are product and partnership constraints for firms operating between Washington and Beijing.

articles.title: K-shaped America and elite mobility narratives
articles.idea: Elite cosmopolitan mobility stories can mask domestic distribution fights. Founder optionality and median household constraints are different ledgers.

articles.title: Remittance corridors still legitimize SEA payments
articles.idea: Family money moving across borders remains the demand that makes many payment products politically and commercially real in Southeast Asia.

articles.title: The partner is often the product
articles.idea: For first-country entry in Southeast Asia, local equity, licenses, and last-mile control frequently matter more than a translated landing page.

articles.title: Data localization is an architecture rule
articles.idea: Southeast Asia does not share one data-sovereignty regime. Where personal data must live changes vendors, latency budgets, and go-live order.

articles.title: Super-app templates hit national rails
articles.idea: Chinese platform design still influences Southeast Asia. Copying WeChat’s all-in-one stack fails when payments and identity stay national.

articles.title: Founder visas are strategy
articles.idea: Pass thresholds in Singapore and entrepreneur parole rules in the United States allocate where companies incorporate, hire, and raise.

articles.title: Friendshoring reallocates chip attention to SEA
articles.idea: U.S. industrial policy does not only build American fabs. It changes which Southeast Asian nodes get capital and diplomatic focus.

articles.title: Islamic finance is market access
articles.idea: In Malaysia’s system, Shariah-compliant banking and capital markets are large enough to be infrastructure. Product design has to fit them.

articles.title: City-state models fail the archipelago
articles.idea: What works in Singapore density does not transfer to Indonesia logistics by renaming the market “SEA.”

articles.title: US campus pipelines still sort SEA founder talent
articles.idea: US universities and post-study work rules form an institutional pipeline for Southeast Asian founders and engineers. The pipeline is policy-built, not accidental — and it is not the only talent system that matters.

articles.title: SEA family capital into US tech has a Singapore address
articles.idea: Family wealth from Southeast Asia that reaches US private tech markets often travels through Singapore’s regulated fund and family-office schemes. That is cross-border strategy with a rulebook, not anonymous LP money with no institutional home.

articles.title: Chinese EV chains in SEA are political bargains
articles.idea: Battery and EV foreign investment in Southeast Asia is a bargain over minerals, jobs, and industrial policy. The plant is the visible layer. The export ban and the offtake politics are the load-bearing ones.

articles.title: DEFA is not the law founders ship against
articles.idea: ASEAN’s Digital Economy Framework Agreement is a regional project with political timelines. Product teams still ship against national statutes and bilateral digital economy agreements that already bind.

articles.title: English founder media is not the customer
articles.idea: English-language startup coverage in Southeast Asia is good at pricing attention and capital. It is a thin gauge of who pays at checkout.
articles.source: fleet full rewrite 2026-07-31; promoted to /us-asean-china/posts/ on 2026-08-03

articles.title: Basing politics is a data-center site factor
articles.idea: Southeast Asia’s cloud and cable map sits next to alliance geography. Military access agreements and undersea-cable security politics are site factors for digital infrastructure, even when sales decks never say so.

articles.title: Dual-use founders inherit continuous export screening
articles.idea: For firms that touch US technology controls while operating through Southeast Asia, sanctions and export rules are product and ops constraints. A Singapore address does not put the company outside the net.

articles.title: Tourism recovery reloads SME payment seasonality
articles.idea: As visitors return to Southeast Asian destinations, small merchants meet a payments problem that is seasonal, cross-border, and increasingly QR-native. National rails — not only private wallets — now sit in the middle of the trip.

articles.title: Halal certification is export infrastructure
articles.idea: For food, cosmetics, and related goods entering large Muslim-majority markets, the certificate is part of SKU readiness. It sits next to safety standards, not next to the brand deck.

articles.title: Climate risk is ag supply-chain risk
articles.idea: Physical climate stress on Southeast Asian farm belts shows up as yield risk, export risk, and finance risk on the same season clock.

articles.title: Port competition is a services stack fight
articles.idea: Strait hubs re-allocate containers and the bunkering, registry, and trade services that ride on them. Singapore still leads on TEUs. Peers are closing ranks.

articles.title: Diaspora angels as soft capital markets
articles.idea: Organized angel networks and overseas professionals move early equity and introductions across borders. That rail is related to remittances—and is not the same thing.

articles.title: Moderation is a SEA go-to-market risk
articles.idea: National speech and intermediary laws force local workflows. A single global trust-and-safety policy is incomplete product architecture.

articles.title: Edtech export is system design
articles.idea: US and Singapore learning products enter Southeast Asia through universities, exams, and teacher labor markets. Localization of UI is the smaller half of the job.

articles.title: Returns rewrite cross-border margins
articles.idea: Outbound ads and bonded warehouses get the headlines. Reverse logistics and multi-country customs decide whether the order was profit.

articles.title: MAS Granted Coinbase's Wholesale Asks and Held the Line on Retail
articles.idea: Hassan Ahmed's April 2025 Coinbase blog post asked Singapore for seven policy moves. Fifteen months later, the wholesale asks shipped and the retail asks did not — a split too consistent to read as a stall.
articles.source: podcast-prep fleet 2026-08-03 (Hassan Ahmed / Coinbase, NUS FinTech Lab, 6 Aug 2026)
